C2.one_time: Excluded from adjusted: EV strategic realignment $238M pre-tax (vs $1.592B a year ago) and a $208M tax benefit from a change to a subsidiary's legal entity tax classification, so GAAP EPS ($3.73) is above adjusted ($3.70) (8-K Ex 99.1, EPS reconciliation). Inside adjusted: GMNA equity income includes a gain from the sale of an equity investment, amount not disclosed (8-K footnote c); the call cited a $600M Q3 warranty benefit and about $500M of IEEPA tariff refunds credited to earnings, with the quarter split of the refund not stated in the sources read; about $100M negative Momenta mark in GMI (Investing.com transcript; gloom.sh summary). C2.organic: GMNA wholesale 870k vs 840k (+3.6%); GMI wholesale 159k vs 137k. U.S. total sales 671k vs 710k (-5.5%), share 16.1% vs 16.8%; U.S. trucks 359k vs 369k, crossovers 300k vs 330k. Fleet share of total sales 19.2% vs 16.7%. China JV sales 358k vs 469k (-24%) (8-K Ex 99.1, vehicle sales tables). Call: full-size pickup sales up 9% (gloom.sh summary). Analysis: revenue growth came from wholesale timing and mix, not retail demand; U.S. retail volume and share fell and fleet mix rose.
C2.margin_drivers: Call: GMNA gains from richer full-size pickup mix, lower EV losses and lower warranty, offset by commodities (including logistics and DRAM) and onshoring costs. Commodities, logistics and DRAM about $700M in Q3, about $1.3B YTD, about $2B for FY26. EV losses expected down $1B to $1.5B for FY26. NA pricing up $400M YTD (Investing.com transcript; Yahoo Finance call summary). Ultium Cells equity income was insignificant vs $213M a year ago (8-K footnote b).
C2.cash_conversion: Automotive operating cash flow $8.049B; capex $2.333B; adjusted automotive FCF $5.882B, about 143% of EBIT-adjusted. YTD adjusted FCF $12.184B, with $4.242B of EV realignment cash added back (8-K Ex 99.1). Call: Q3 FCF helped by tariff timing. Automotive cash $18.765B plus marketable securities $4.351B at Sep 30 (8-K balance sheet).
C2.share_count_tax: Diluted weighted shares 887M vs 910M in Q2 and 964M a year ago; 849M shares outstanding at Sep 30 vs 904M at end 2025 (8-K Ex 99.1). Buyback $2.5B in Q3, $1B more in October, $6.3B YTD, prior $6.0B program completed; new $20B multi-year authorization (release; call). ETR-adjusted 19.9% vs 19.8% (8-K). No named bottleneck components and no supplier co-investment commitment.
C4.new_info: Preliminary 2027 WFE above $200B; 2026 WFE raised to mid $150B; 2026 systems revenue growth 'well over 40%'; CSBG growth above 30% in 2026 and above 15% in 2027; some December revenue moves to March on supply; China down meaningfully in December; tax 16.5% continuing; NAND up about 40% Q/Q with early 384-layer spending; Aether about $2.5B by decade-end; ASR under way with about $3B authorization left; inventory turns 3.4x (Stifel question). China 'meaningfully down' in December with no number; mid-50s gross margin 'over the next several years', near term 'bounce around generally where it is', with new products, close-to-customer manufacturing and pricing as the levers; tax 16.5% (Call transcript (Investing.com, AI-assisted, 10/21/2026)).

C7.suppliers_customers: Analysis: Lam named component supply and customer clean room timing as the constraint, which points to equipment-component suppliers and fab construction schedules as the items to watch. Memory makers (DRAM leads 2027 growth) are the customers whose capex plans matter most. No specific supplier or customer was named on the call (Call transcript (Investing.com, AI-assisted, 10/21/2026)).
C7.theme: Analysis: the sector story moved from 'is AI spending pausing' (9/14 scare) to 'can the supply chain deliver'. Lam saw no demand pause; the stock still fell on the print.

C8.thesis_in: From A4: (1) 2027 WFE is still a growth year despite the AI-pacing scare; (2) the NAND upgrade cycle cannot keep doubling and needs new capacity plus DRAM/HBM to take over; (3) gross margin can move from 52% toward mid-50s while China shrinks.
C8.changed: Debate 1 settled yes: preliminary 2027 WFE above $200B, led by DRAM, and no pushouts mentioned; the limit is supply, not demand (Call transcript (Investing.com, AI-assisted, 10/21/2026)). Debate 2 partly settled: NAND rose about 40% Q/Q, but CSBG was flat Q/Q; conversions finish in 2027 and roll into the next upgrade cycle; CSBG growth slows to above 15% in 2027 (Call transcript (Investing.com, AI-assisted, 10/21/2026); Release (8-K Ex 99.1, 10/21/2026)). Debate 3 went the other way on China: China rose to 35% yet gross margin still rose to 52.4%, December guided to 52.5%, mid-50s is a multi-year target, and the risk A4 named (tax, supply) is what showed up. Analysis: demand case stronger, near-term revenue conversion weaker than the bull case.

C12.bottom_line: Lam beat by about 1% on revenue ($8.22B vs $8.14B) and EPS ($2.20 vs $2.17 to $2.18), and guided December to $8.60B and $2.33, within 1% of the Street, saying supply constraints held the guide down. qa.q: Has SpaceX ordered EUV machines and when do they arrive; where can the chip fab supply chain be improved?
qa.real_q: How real and how soon is Terafab?
qa.a: Internal aim: a functional SRAM test chip around May or June 2027 at the Austin research fab; volume production around Q3 2028 at Gibbons Creek, possibly Q4 2028, with 'big error bars'. Thanked ASML and suppliers for pulling equipment forward. Would not discuss process breakthroughs

qa.q: How are you solving power, cooling and infrastructure, what gives you comfort in 13 GW by end of 2027, and how will it be funded?
qa.real_q: Is 13 GW credible and what does it cost the balance sheet?
qa.a: Musk: close to 3 GW within months; a 'highly proprietary' plan for 20 GW of incremental power and cooling in 2027; SpaceX casts its own turbine blades and vanes, which suppliers deliver 12 to 18 months late; highly confident of 10 GW incremental. Johnsen: investment grade, several debt pools in discussion, short payback, operating cash flow, vendor and customer partnerships. No dollar figure

qa.q: What are the pros and cons of combining with Tesla, and what roadblocks would need to be addressed?
qa.real_q: Is a Tesla merger coming and on what terms?
qa.a: Both companies formed special committees of independent directors at shareholders' request; Musk is conflicted and not in the talks; a merger is not a certainty; Tesla needs 50% of all shares outstanding to vote yes; the committees have not agreed terms. Musk thinks combining makes sense (SI software, chip design, Terafab, robotics, Starmind)

qa.q: What roles do the satellite and terrestrial layers play in Starlink Mobile, what is the traffic mix for a 5G-like US experience, and how much of the focus is retail wireless vs physical AI?
qa.real_q: Is the spectrum enough to compete with the US carriers?
qa.a: Shotwell: 85% to 93% of mobile traffic runs on WiFi; S-band carries the majority, 800 MHz low band handles building penetration; small radios on existing Starlink installs and towers. Musk: a clear path to several hundred billion dollars a year of connectivity revenue, details at a later presentation. No traffic split, physical AI not addressed

qa.q: How do you balance compute between external cloud services and internal needs (Cursor, Grok Bot), and what does the mix mean for monetization over 12 to 18 months?
qa.real_q: How much of the compute is rented out, and at what price?
qa.a: Goal about 50/50, could swing to 60/40 either way, month to month; rent at spot rates on short contracts rather than long deals; renewals at higher dollars per watt; could rent the capacity several times over; a six-month payback next year is 'not impossible'. No revenue or margin figure for the mix

qa.q: When will V3 capacity show up as faster speeds and lower latency, and how many V3 satellites are needed?
qa.a: Shotwell: a few hundred V3 satellites, which she expects by mid 2027

qa.q: What is the Starbase Louisiana timeline and the confidence in a first Starship launch there as early as 2029?
qa.a: Musk: internal aim is 2028; 2029 highly likely, at scale in 2029. The release says first launch targeted for 2029

C8.changed: Analysis: the AI debate moved toward the bull case. SI turned profitable ($431M operating income, $4.95B segment adjusted EBITDA), management claims payback under a year, and the Q1 2027 guide of $33B to $37B makes Street 2027 revenue look low. Starlink ARPU rose to $69 instead of falling, though net adds of 1.6M fell short of the 2M bull mark. Against that, capex roughly doubles to $35B to $40B in Q4, Q3 free cash flow was about -$10B, Q4 gross margin steps down about 7 points, and part of the EPS beat came from $1.03B of other income and a $390M tax benefit. C12.bottom_line: Analysis: SpaceX beat on every headline line and, more important, guided Q1 2027 revenue to $33B to $37B, which shows SI compute can earn a profit and leaves Street 2027 numbers too low. The cost is a Q4 capex bill of $35B to $40B and negative free cash flow funded with debt, and part of the EPS beat came below the line. The stock's +7.8% was a little larger than the 7% implied move; the next tests are Flight 15, the December run rate and the 12/8 lockup.
